papers.title: The Industrialization of Cognition
papers.subtitle: Transformed
papers.abstract: Organisations with high AI adoption are producing roughly twice the code of low adopters. They are completing about 27% more work. Hyundai cut digital-twin construction from four weeks to ten days and still cannot justify rolling it out globally, because integration across mismatched robot and PLC vendors doubles the engineering it saved. Insilico reaches a drug candidate in nine months against a traditional baseline near four and a half years, and then waits on clinical trials exactly as long as everyone else. Four industries, four instruments, one measurement. Generation is accelerating fast

papers.title: Execution-Boundary Governance
papers.subtitle: A Runtime Control Model for Autonomous Systems
papers.abstract: Current AI governance frameworks focus on policy, oversight, documentation, transparency, and post-execution accountability. As autonomous systems gain the ability to execute transactions, invoke tools, modify records, move funds, and trigger physical actions, governance must operate within finite latency budgets. This paper proposes Execution-Boundary Governance (EBG), a framework that distinguishes interpretive governance from executable governance and introduces the Executable Governance Kernel (EGK) — a minimal, deterministic, tamper-resistant mechanism operating at the final control point

papers.title: Upstream
papers.subtitle: Where Human-in-the-Loop Goes at Machine Speed
papers.abstract: Software now takes consequential action on its own. It places orders, moves money, approves claims, and grants access, and it does all of it faster than anyone can review. Governance that cannot be present at the moment of action has to be settled beforehand, and written so a machine can apply it without asking. This paper examines what happens when organisations try to do that at scale. The usual conclusion is that the human leaves the loop. That conclusion is wrong. papers.title: The Execution Surface
papers.subtitle: Why Distributed Compute Cannot Be Shared
papers.abstract: Compute is moving outward. That argument is over, and this paper does not make it. It starts from the condition itself and asks what kind of thing is being built. The answer is a planetary execution surface: a continuous layer of local compute running from gigawatt campuses down to milliwatt endpoints, thickest wherever consequences occur. papers.title: Machine-Speed Economics
papers.subtitle: How Evidence Becomes the Price Signal
papers.abstract: An economy is buyers meeting sellers, prices moving, and obligations settling — with enough reliability that strangers will trade. This paper describes that economy with the humans removed from the middle of each transaction, and argues that what makes it possible is not faster money but independently witnessed evidence. The paper makes six claims. First, the machine-speed economy requires nothing that does not already exist. Agents carry a purse — bounded spending authority committable at the point of action — and a mandate — preconstrained limits on what may be done, for whom, at what cost.
